verdict.rationale: Twilio documents an official MCP server at twilio.com/docs/ai/mcp that AI coding agents connect to from the IDE, with structured access to over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products. However, the docs say it indexes public API specifications only and needs no account or keys, so the evidence does not show agents acting on a live Twilio account through it. missing for 10: evidence of authenticated account-level operations via the MCP server, client setup/configuration details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: gives AI coding agents direct, structured access to Twilio's full API surface—over 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products—without leaving your IDE.
The MCP server indexes public API specifications only. No Twilio account or API keys needed.
official MCP server documented at https://www.twilio.com/docs/ai/mcp
